data.why: A gas stove stands cut open in a kitchen; the gas is followed from the pipe through the knob, the burner tube and the head to the flame under a pot, and a hand on the knob comes back at each human step. The camera opens close on the pipe and the pot, then frames each added part and goes close where the pot scorches and the spark clicks.

chain.shows: the open pipe roars a flame that never stops
the gas from the knob burns yellow and blackens the pot with soot
chain.stakes: the pot and kitchen get sooty

chain.shows: the tube's thin blue flame scorches one red spot on the pot
chain.stakes: the food burns in the middle

chain.shows: a draft blows the ring out and gas leaks into the kitchen
with the gas shut by the sensor, the burner stays dark until a match
chain.stakes: lighting it by hand is risky

surprises.claim: A gas flame burns blue when air is mixed into the gas before it burns; without enough air it burns yellow and makes soot.
surprises.search: gas stove yellow flame soot not enough air blue flame

surprises.claim: A flame failure device shuts off the gas if a burner's flame goes out.
surprises.search: gas hob flame failure device thermocouple shuts off gas flame goes out

surprises.claim: Most gas stoves light with an electric spark igniter that clicks.
surprises.search: gas stove spark igniter clicking how it lights

ideas.idea: lighting gas from a pipe under a pot is already a stove
the gas never stops, the flame roars all day
a knob on a valve turns the gas down
gas burning without air is a lazy yellow flame that blackens the pot
a burner tube pulls air in through its holes, so the gas burns blue
the tube's one thin flame burns one spot
a burner head spreads the flame into a ring
a draft blows the ring out and raw gas leaks
a flame sensor shuts the gas when the flame dies
with the gas shut, relighting needs a match
a spark igniter clicks it alight
turn the knob and the blue ring heats the pot

sentences.text: If you light gas from a pipe under a pot, you have a stove.
But the gas never stops, and the flame roars.
So you add a knob to turn it down.
But the lazy yellow flame coats the pot in soot.
So a burner tube mixes air into the gas.
But the tube's blue flame scorches one spot.
So a burner head spreads it into a ring.
But a draft blows the ring out, and gas leaks.
So a sensor shuts the gas when the flame dies.
But now lighting it takes a match.
So a spark igniter clicks it alight.
Turn the knob, and blue flames heat your pot.
Congratulations, you built a gas stove.
